segments.text: Now on the country, next shloka, yadātu pārmeśi shakti pārta vāsi unmishitam samsabhāma mev yumrashati,
when on the country the grace of Lord Shiva is infused in his consciousness,
pārmeśi shakti pārta vāsi unmishitam, and that by infusion samsabhāma mev yumrashati when he contemplates
and realizes his own nature, intrusions, then Abhilāshā bāvāt, he destroys all desires in himself,
no asa bairgati, he does not move towards outside the world.
Aptu, on the country, ātmārāmatā ivanitam, he is always centered in his own God consciousness.
That is what he explains in this shloka.
Tadārūd premityais tāth kēyāt jīv sun kēyā.
That person, that fortunate person whose consciousness is established in his own real nature,
tāth means real nature.
Tāth rūd premityais, premityais consciousness, whose consciousness is established in his own nature,
then what happens to him, tāth kēyāt, desire vanishes in him, all desires vanishes in him,
jīv sun kēyā.
So, there is no jīv, jīv, jīv or disappear in him.
The state of being individual, individual is finished.
Tāth hiti, he explains what is the meaning of tāth.
Pūru nirdiśta samvētrāthmini tūri padē.
As previously, in previous sutras, we have explained that state of tūriya,
which is only no-ver, the state of no-ver, not known or knowledge.
Only no-ver, the state of no-ver, samvētri, samvētrāthmini tūri padē.
When aura tāth vimarsana pāra premityais, samvētri, whose consciousness is established in other words,
tāth vimarsana pāra, whose consciousness is fully air in that Supreme God consciousness.
Then tāth hiti, abilājī kēyāt, then that desire is vanished.
That desire, which seems to be existing there, that vanishes jīvāsya and jīvāva individuality is finished.
Jīvāsya, what is the meaning of jīvāsya, samvētri padē, samvētri padē, samvētri padē.
That state of being aware of purheśtaka, state of being aware that I am purheśtaka,
I am body, I am organs, I am mind, intellect and ego.
That state is over, that means prasama.
It is a piece, it is shānta.
Jīvāsya, tāvāsya, suprati.
On the contrary, his pramātrita, his consciousness,
shines in jīt, in jīt, in his own nature.
Yaduhtam tātravā, it is said in that kālikā kram.
Yatāsānu bhūt, supranānu bhūtārthān, prabhuddho nāyupāśiti, tātā bāvaneya, yogī, samsāran, nāyupāśiti.
When one is experiencing the dreaming state and he perceives so many dreams, various dreams,
various ways of dreams, world of dreams, in dreaming state, when he gets out of it,
when he enters in wakefulness, then those all dreams are all together.
They vanish altogether. No dream is existing at all.
In the same way, tātā bāvaneya, yogī, samsāran, nāyupāśiti, even yogī,
fortunate yogī puts awareness in this way, on this objective world of universe,
that this universe is not objective world. It is only subjective consciousness, nothing else.
And the more he puts awareness on subjective consciousness, he becomes one with subjective consciousness.
So, this imagination also becomes true for him.
By and by, by and by, you put your awareness in this imagination that this whole universe is nothing,
by but my own self nature. Go on meditating on it in continuation and time will come,
he will become one with that god consciousness.
Bhāvaneya. Bhāvaneya. Bhāvaneya is last realization.
Bhāvaneya is to confuse awareness, to put awareness in continuity.
Nērāsādhsādhsādhvṛti samsṛtiya padam antaram vihai kalpanājālam adhaita-yena parāparam.
These states which are existing and states which are not existing, you should avoid them.
Avoid these two states existing and non-existent states.
Hold that state which is internally established in your own nature.
Samsṛtiya padam antaram vihai kalpanājālam and remove away all these classes of kalpanājālam imagination.
By putting adhaita, by putting oneness, one god consciousness in present, yes.
Yes, samsṛtiya padam antaram vihai kalpanājālam and remove away all these classes of kalpanājālam.
That person who is established in his own nature, always, nityam.
And kalpanājālam and remove away all these classes of kalpanājālam and remove away all these classes of kalpanājālam.
Kal does not mean death. He wants to destroy this fear of time.
By putting consciousness on the timeless point.
Timeless point is found between two breaths. Timeless point is found between one step and another step.
One talk and another talk, one word and another word.
In between, there is timeless point. That is called agra-sikrta.
When your consciousness is bent upon finding out that point, then you are said to be called agra-sikrta.
You are bent upon destroying this fear of time.
So, in near future, there will be no time existing for you.
Kaivalipadabhā-hyogi. So, that hyogi is established in that final bititude of god consciousness.
And so, nirvāna padam labhēt, he achieves that state of nirvāna, moksha, final liberation.
Kaivalipadabhā-hyogi. In this shloka, Kaival, what is the meaning of Kaivalipadabhā-hyogi?
Final liberation. Yandre-tanmatra-bir-asamvāya.
He does not become the object of being carried. He becomes carrier.
He carries everyone. He is not carried by anybody from one state to another state.
